data.name: Narsingh
data.short_meaning: Lord Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu
data.long_meaning: Narsingh is a name that signifies the divine manifestation of Lord Vishnu as Narasimha, the man-lion. This powerful and courageous avatar is believed to protect devotees from their inner and outer enemies. The name Narsingh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'nar' meaning man and 'singh' meaning lion. It is a symbol of strength, courage, and protection.
data.spiritual_meaning: Narsingh represents the divine power that protects and upholds dharma (righteousness) in the world. It is a reminder that no matter how powerful the challenges we face in life, we can always find strength and courage within ourselves, with the grace of the divine.
data.numerology_meaning: Narsingh is a name with the Life Path Number 8, which indicates a strong will, power, and the ability to achieve great things in life. It also signifies a talent for business, leadership, and a desire for material success.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The story of Narsingh is mentioned in the Hindu epics, Mahabharata and Ramayana. The name Narsingh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Narsingh is considered an avatar of the god Vishnu. In the Mahabharata, he appears as the protector of the Yadava clan and later as a man-lion to kill the demon Trivakrama. In the Ramayana, he appears to save Lord Rama from the demon Hiranyakasipu when he takes the form of a man with the head of a lion.

historical_references.reference: Another version of the Narsingh story is told in the Puranas, which describes his role as the destroyer of the demon Hiranyakashipu, father of Hiranyakasipu.
historical_references.context: In this version, Narsingh appears as a half-man, half-lion form to kill Hiranyakashipu, who had gained a boon that he could not be killed by man or beast, deva or asura, indoors or outdoors. Narsingh, invoking his divine power, appeared in a form that fulfilled none of these conditions, allowing him to destroy the demon.
